source.title: Every Ablation Is a Dose: Counterweights and the Semblance of Self-Repair
source.authors: Areeb Ahmad; Pratinav Seth; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some equations and tables have PDF-extraction formatting artifacts.
record.tranche_reason: Tests IOI head effects under a dose-controlled, nested activation-patching intervention, rather than using the original circuit-discovery evaluation. It also measures how the results vary under another reference convention.
record.gate_note: The IOI section uses Wang et al.'s published circuit as its component bench and reports results on reachable heads, upstream heads, and mean-ablation dose placement. Statements about results from other papers are not included as rows. The study does not retest the complete 26-head circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.test_reason: In GPT-2 small on IOI, the study doses the name-mover pair L9.h6+L9.h9 continuously toward the counterfactual. It then measures how each downstream circuit head's contribution to the logit difference changes. Backup and other name movers rise as the core's signal is removed, which is the V2 self-repair effect measured on a dose axis rather than by a single ablation. The authors restate V2: the takeover is the release of a linear coupling already active in the clean model, not recruitment. The 26-head circuit is used as a fixed bench and is not retested, so V1 and V3–V6 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that 7 of the 10 reachable IOI heads follow the affine dose law, and all 7 are counterweights (no relays). L10.h7 (copy suppression) has by far the strongest coupling. The backup reported by Wang et al. is the release of a coupling already active in the clean model, not new recruitment. L11.h10's curvature is mediated by L10.h7, and coupling strength is legible in query weights.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a controlled dose ladder and nested, regime-consistent activation patching to fit head contributions, rather than reproducing the original circuit's faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Under a second reference convention all ten reachable heads certify rather than seven, with held-out median |z| changing from 0.23 to 0.41. Mean-ablation dose placement also differs between the two core heads: 40% versus 8% of pairs fall outside |λ| ≤ 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean ablation of the core lands at a per-pair dose: median about 0 for both heads, but 40% (L9.h6) vs 8% (L9.h9) of pairs fall outside |λ|≤1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conventional ablations of IOI heads deliver uncalibrated, pair-varying intervention strengths.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a second reference convention, all 10 reachable heads certify instead of 7, and held-out median |z| rises from 0.23 to 0.41.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dose-response certification of IOI heads depends on the reference convention.

fits_no_version.finding: Query-composition alignment of the core's write with each head's query predicts |γ| (ρ=+0.818); key and value channels are null.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backup coupling strength in the IOI circuit is readable from query weights.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says code and per-run outputs will be released with the camera-ready version.
record.problems: The IOI test uses one model, one task, one template, and 300 prompt pairs. Only ten reachable heads are fitted; the full 26-head circuit and its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria are not retested. The half-rung holdout is interpolation, and the authors say it establishes smoothness rather than selecting the affine form over other smooth alternatives. A second reference convention changes the number of certified heads.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numerical IOI head results were omitted. Figure 31's dose distributions are recorded as the two mean-ablation rows; figure-only display details not stated numerically in the text are not extracted.

untested.parts: All: Wang's circuit is used as a fixed bench; the 26 heads, 7 classes, and faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not retested.
Recovery of logit difference or accuracy under full ablation of all name movers. L10.h0 is not in the dosed core, and no conventional ablation result is reported for the backups.
All: one model, one task, no checkpoints.
All: no alternative circuit-discovery methods are compared.
No faithfulness or completeness metric is computed under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
All: a single template; swapping the names is the pairing method, not a variant test; no extra names.

missing.what: Refit without the λ=+1 rung: two reachable heads stop certifying and L8.h10 starts certifying.
Query-composition vs |γ| correlation across the ten reachable heads (ρ=0.818, p=0.0056; 0.917 without L11.h10).
Clamping L10.h7 changes the other recruits' slopes only by factors 0.73–1.08.

record.verdict_notes: The IOI arm is an out-of-domain appendix (§L) to a factual-verdict paper. The core dosed is only L9.h6+L9.h9, so L10.h0 acts as a free name mover. L11.h10's two-head-core slope is reported as −0.0348 in Table 31 but −0.0701 in §L.3/Fig. 29, apparently from different reference ladders. The record's V1 and V6 links rest on using the circuit's roles and the method's name swap, which do not test those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Does not retest the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, or minimality criteria; tests dose responses for selected circuit heads.
Does not measure generated IOI answer accuracy as a takeover rate; tests causal contributions of selected heads after intervening on the name-mover core.
Does not test whether the same IOI circuit occurs in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether its components are reused for other tasks.
Does not compare independent circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics. The alternate reference convention is not a comparison of circuit-finding methods.

Does not systematically vary the prompt distribution or compare circuit-level faithfulness and completeness metrics; its IOI sensitivity evidence concerns dose placement and a second reference convention.
Tests paired IOI prompts with the two names exchanged, but not multiple templates or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Dose-swap the core L9.h6 + L9.h9 and measure the head's nested counterfactual contribution; fit a shared slope over |λ| ≤ 1.
rows.note: Certified after Benjamini-Hochberg correction; the authors identify it as the copy-suppression head and the strongest coupling.
rows.check: Linked to V1/V6 wrongly. A slope measures the response to the core dose, not circuit faithfulness, and the name swap is the method, not a prompt-variant test. Negative name mover L10.h7 (gamma −0.886) weakens its opposition as the core is removed, part of Wang et al.'s self-repair pattern.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: Measure response to the core dose swap for heads the intervention cannot reach.

conditions.value: 10 circuit heads in layer 8 and earlier

rows.measure: Head coupling and change in contribution
rows.value: No outside head certifies; six of twelve do not move (max |Eπ − E0| < 10−3); among six that move, median |γr| = 4.5×10−3
rows.note: The twelve comprise the ten layer-8-and-earlier heads and two same-layer heads excluded from the reachable-head fits.
rows.check: A placement control for the coupling law: heads upstream of the core cannot be reached, so their silence follows from layer order. It does not test V1. §L.6 says the honest separation is about eightfold, not tenfold, and that dropping the λ=+1 rung makes L8.h10 certify.

relationships.display_finding: Compensation varied linearly with dose through the clean point, indicating release of existing coupling rather than reactive recruitment; its apparent magnitude depended on ablation dose.

source_check.notes: §L.6 reports that all ten reachable heads certify under a second reference convention used by the factual ladders; the IOI figures use another convention, so describing these particular results as regime-consistent is misleading. statements.correction: §7: increased backup contributions interpreted as release of existing coupling. V2: compensation after main-head ablation; no requirement of newly recruited functionality.
statements.problem: The authors' mechanistic interpretation is accurately reported, but standing coupling alone does not limit V2, which does not require reactive recruitment.
